subject: MAP: Success criteria, exit gates & smoke tests for Orchard pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@orchardanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Success criteria, exit gates & smoke tests for Orchard pilot

Sanjay —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together a short mutual action plan draft that codifies the success criteria and the concrete acceptance tests our teams will run during the pilot. The goal is to make the close decision data-driven and avoid any last-minute scope surprises.

High level (please skim):
- Objective: Validate real-time triage throughput and clinical labeling quality for Orchard’s inbound notes pipeline.
- Exit gates: 1) >= 92% label-level F1 on the evaluation testset for primary diagnosis extraction; 2) sustained 95th pct latency <= 120ms for 512-token generation under 50 RPS during observation window; 3) no SEV1 reliability incidents for 5 consecutive business days.
- Acceptance tests: unit eval suite (attached), two production-like smoke runs (one with 1k-record batch, one with live traffic sampling), and an evidence notebook for audit.

Requested next steps:
1) Tell me if these gates match what your stakeholders will accept or suggest edits.
2) Confirm target week for joint smoke testing (we proposed Apr 24–28).
3) Share a participant list for the verification calls (ops, security, product).

I attached: Orchard_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), acceptance-smoke-scripts.md (test shell), latency-sla-sample.csv (example telemetry labels).

If this all looks good I’ll move the MAP to HubSpot and send a calendar for the kickoff working session.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0143

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@orchardanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: pilot-team@orchardanalytics.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Success criteria, exit gates & smoke tests for Orchard pilot

Marissa —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and clear framing. Quick alignment from our side:
- F1 target: we can accept 92% on the current curated testset; we’ll also require a secondary check on a random holdout (10% unseen) to ensure generalization.
- Latency: 120ms at 50 RPS is reasonable as a target; we’ll ask for an additional 99th pct telemetry line in the report.
- Reliability: 5 business days with zero SEV1 is fine; we’ll require an on-call contact and an incident playback template.

Two asks before we lock week Apr 24–28:
1) Can you confirm whether the smoke runs will use our redacted production backlog or synthetic data?
2) We need the MAP to call out data retention and audit log access for compliance reviewers.

I’ll loop in product and security this afternoon for any redlines, but overall we’re aligned.

—Sanjay Rao
Head of Product, Orchard Analytics
sanjay@orchardanalytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@orchardanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Success criteria, exit gates & smoke tests for Orchard pilot

On Sat, Apr 3, 2027 at 9:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sanjay —
> 
> Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together a short mutual action plan draft that codifies the success criteria and the concrete acceptance tests our teams will run during the pilot.

Thanks for the prompt confirmation and the asks — good calls. Quick clarifications and updates in the attached v1.1:
- Data for smoke runs: we will run two modes — (A) redacted production backlog (preferred) behind your consented QA window, and (B) synthetic parity dataset if security requires. The MAP includes both flows and explicit gating for the redacted-backlog run.
- Audit / retention: added a section that lists the audit artifacts we’ll provide post-run (request logs, token-level access traces, and the evidence notebook). Per our policy we can offer a 90-day ephemeral trace view for compliance review; longer retention is an enterprise add-on.
- 99th pct latency: added to the telemetry artifact list and included a sample column in latency-sla-sample.csv.

I also added a simple pass/fail rubric for each acceptance test (file: acceptance-smoke-scripts.md) and a runbook owner mapping.

Next concrete items from Redwood:
- Kickoff working session invite (1 hour) once you confirm Apr 24 or Apr 26.
- Shared runbook in Drive + a join link for the smoke runs.
- On-call contact for the pilot: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.com).

If that aligns I’ll push the MAP to HubSpot and attach the runbook links.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@orchardanalytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Success criteria, exit gates & smoke tests for Orchard pilot

Following up with a couple technical caveats for the MAP (quick bullets):
- Load shape: please expect brief microbursts during the redacted-backlog run; we recommend a warmed KV cache and a pre-run steady-load warmup (15 minutes) to avoid cold-start latencies affecting the 99th pct.
- Test harness: we’ll provide a small harness that emits synthetic jitter to simulate network egress; I attached a sample CSV for telemetry and will drop the harness script into the shared Drive later today.
- Rollback trigger: added a rollback condition when label-level F1 drops >4 percentage points between consecutive runs (this is in the MAP workbook).

Ben (on-call for this pilot)
Ben Carter | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0192

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@orchardanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, pilot-team@orchardanalytics.com
Date: 2027-04-05T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Success criteria, exit gates & smoke tests for Orchard pilot

Marissa / Ben —

All looks good on our side. We prefer Apr 26 for the kickoff (gives security time for the redaction checklist). Two confirmations:
1) We accept the rollback trigger as you described.
2) Please add the incident playback template to the Drive folder before Apr 20 so our compliance reviewer can pre-check.

Once you push the MAP to HubSpot well mark the deal as in-pilot and Ill share the final participant list.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

—Sanjay
Head of Product, Orchard Analytics
